# DSH Studio v0.7.2

This patch release fixes the post-install Contract 2 false negative in v0.7.1
and gives one-click update checks a validated official fallback.

## Added

- Update checks try the GitHub Release `latest.json` and then the official
  `https://moresyl.github.io/dsh-studio/latest.json` fallback.
- Contract failures name the exact missing condition instead of repeating only
  the Harness and pnpm versions that were found.
- Package-channel publishing copies `latest.json` to Pages only after checking
  the exact version, HTTPS artifact URLs and every Tauri signature.

## Changed and secured

- First install, update and Repair pass npm `--install-links`, materializing
  `@moresyl/dsh-studio-integration` instead of depending on a Windows junction
  into the temporary install source.
- Release metadata fetches use bounded retries for transient resets. Pages is a
  manifest fallback only; downloaded applications still require Studio's
  embedded Tauri public key. The desktop bridge remains Protocol 3.

## Fixed and polished

- Fixed npm completing all 511 packages and Studio then rejecting Contract 2.
  A Windows cold-install regression proves that the integration is a real
  directory and that the resulting `dsh --help` executes.
- A failed primary update check no longer exposes only the raw request error.
  Studio tries the fallback and otherwise explains GitHub,
  `HTTPS_PROXY`, retry and Full / Offline recovery in Chinese and English.

## Install and update

v0.7.1 does not yet know the fallback. If its update check cannot reach GitHub,
install v0.7.2 manually from Assets; prefer Full / Offline on an unreliable
connection. Lite and Full share identity and data directories and preserve
existing `~/.dsh` profiles.

Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates still require the Tauri
signature. Windows Authenticode and Apple Developer ID credentials remain
unconfigured, so OS trust warnings are separate from updater and SHA-256 checks.
